readmeExcerpt:
A beautiful, powerful, self-hosted ROM manager and player.


# Overview Scan, enrich, browse and play your ROM collection from one beautiful & free self-hosted app. Metadata from 10+ providers, save sync across your devices, and support for over 400 platforms. RomM is a must-have for anyone who plays on emulators.

## Features - Play in your browser with [EmulatorJS][docs-emulatorjs] and [RuffleRS][docs-rufflers], no setup required - Keep [saves and states][docs-saves] in sync across your devices, with conflict resolution - Scan and enrich your library with metadata from [IGDB][igdb-api], [Screenscraper][screenscraper-api], [LaunchBox][launchbox-api] and [MobyGames][mobygames-api] - Fetch custom artwork from [SteamGridDB][steamgriddb-api] and track your achievements from [Retroachievements][retroachievements-api] - Metadata available for [400+ platforms][docs-supported-platforms], plus multi-disk games, DLCs, mods, hacks and manuals - Apply romhacks and translations on the fly with the built-in [ROM patcher][docs-rom-patcher] - Share your library with granular [per-user permissions][docs-users-and-roles] and [OIDC single sign-on][docs-oidc] - Official apps for [Playnite][playnite-app], [Android][argosy-launcher] and [CFWs][grout] - Free forever: AGPL-3.0, no tracking, no paid features, and total control of your data ## Installation The easiest way to start is with the [Quick Start Guide][docs-quick-start-guide] in the docs. If you're having trouble with setup, please review the page for [troubleshooting steps][docs-troubleshooting]. Prefer a hosted deploy over wiring up the stack yourself?

readmeHtml:
A beautiful, powerful, self-hosted ROM manager and player.


Overview

Scan, enrich, browse and play your ROM collection from one beautiful & free self-hosted app. Metadata from 10+ providers, save sync across your devices, and support for over 400 platforms. RomM is a must-have for anyone who plays on emulators.

Features

  • Play in your browser with EmulatorJS and RuffleRS, no setup required
  • Keep saves and states in sync across your devices, with conflict resolution
  • Scan and enrich your library with metadata from IGDB, Screenscraper, LaunchBox and MobyGames
  • Fetch custom artwork from SteamGridDB and track your achievements from Retroachievements
  • Metadata available for 400+ platforms, plus multi-disk games, DLCs, mods, hacks and manuals
  • Apply romhacks and translations on the fly with the built-in ROM patcher
  • Share your library with granular per-user permissions and OIDC single sign-on
  • Official apps for Playnite, Android and CFWs
  • Free forever: AGPL-3.0, no tracking, no paid features, and total control of your data

Installation

The easiest way to start is with the Quick Start Guide in the docs. If you're having trouble with setup, please review the page for troubleshooting steps.

Prefer a hosted deploy over wiring up the stack yourself?

*Supports Allium, Batocera, Knulli, MinUI, muOS, NextUI, Onion, ROCKNIX, Spruce and TrimUI.

Here are some cool projects maintained by members of our community. Please note that our team does not regularly review their source code.

Handhelds

  • DeckyRommSync: SteamOS downloader and syncer by @danielcopper
  • SwitchRomM: Homebrew NRO for Switch by @Shalasere

Other

  • romm-comm: Discord bot by @idio-sync

Consider supporting this project on Open Collective. Funds cover hosting, development, and maintenance, and we pass some along to community projects to nurture a healthy ecosystem of apps.

> [!CAUTION]
> ## Breaking changes
> ### Filesystem structure must be explicitly declared
> We no longer detect the filesystem layout by default, and an instance will **refuses to start** until explicitly declared in your `config.yml`. This is the equivalent of **structure A**:
>
> ```yaml
> filesystem:
>   structure:
>     default: "roms/{platform}/{game}"
>     firmware: "bios/{platform}"
> ```
>
> And the equivalent of **structure B**:
>
> ```yaml
> filesystem:
>   structure:
>     default: "{platform}/roms/{game}"
>     firmware: "{platform}/bios"
> ```
>
> `filesystem.roms_folder` and `filesystem.firmware_folder` have also been removed. An instance that still sets either will refuse to start and print the equivalent template.
>
> See [Custom library structure](https://docs.romm.app/5.3.0-alpha/getting-started/folder-structure/#custom-library-structure) and the [`filesystem.structure`](https://docs.romm.app/5.3.0-alpha/reference/configuration-file/#filesystemstructure) schema.

releases.name: 5.3.0-alpha.1
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **Structure B is gone.**
> We no longer detect the `{platform}/roms/` layout, and an instance laid out that way **refuses to start** rather than scanning an empty library and marking every ROM missing. To keep a Structure B library, declare it, and note that it takes two templates:
>
> ```yaml
> filesystem:
>   structure:
>     default: "{platform}/roms/{game}"
>     firmware: "{platform}/bios"
> ```
>
> **`filesystem.roms_folder` and `filesystem.firmware_folder` are gone too.** Each named one path segment that a template now contains, and an instance that still sets either refuses to start, printing the equivalent template to paste:
>
> ```yaml
> filesystem:
>   structure:
>     default: "<your roms_folder>/{platform}/{game}"
>     firmware: "<your firmware_folder>/{platform}"
> ```
>
> See [Custom library structure](https://docs.romm.app/5.3.0-alpha/getting-started/folder-structure/#custom-library-structure) and the [`filesystem.structure`](https://docs.romm.app/5.3.0-alpha/reference/configuration-file/#filesystemstructure) schema.

> [!WARNING]
> **Emulator streaming config is now one entry per container, not one per emulator.**

aiSummary.oneLiner: A self-hosted ROM manager and modern web-based retro game player with rich metadata integration.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Romm is a comprehensive self-hosted platform designed for managing and playing extensive retro video game collections. It scans local directories for ROM files and automatically fetches rich metadata, high-quality cover art, and release information via integrations with databases like IGDB and Screenscraper. The application provides a modern, responsive web interface for organizing, tagging, and browsing the library seamlessly across multiple devices. Crucially, it includes an integrated web-based emulator layer that allows users to play their classic games directly in the browser without installing any local standalone emulators.
keyFeatures: Automated metadata scraping: Fetches high-quality box art, screenshots, and detailed game descriptions from external sources like IGDB.
Integrated web player: Plays classic console games directly within modern web browsers using integrated WebAssembly-based emulator technologies.
Cross-device synchronization: Syncs game save states and play history across desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices effortlessly.
Modern web interface: Offers a beautiful, responsive, and highly customizable user interface for organizing and browsing large game libraries.
Multi-system support: Manages ROMs, ISOs, and patches for dozens of retro consoles and handhelds within a single, unified platform.
